facts.raw_span: A ten-month-old Hispanic girl presented for evaluation of facial asymmetry noted since birth
the right lower lip deviates inward, whereas the rest of facial movement is symmetric
Pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the patient was born full term
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
her face is symmetric at rest
When she smiles, the right lower lip deviates inward
frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides
A neurodevelopmental examination is normal
Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal
echocardiography shows no cardiac anomalies
an auditory brainstem response test reveals normal hearing pathways

concepts.why: The patient's facial asymmetry noted since birth, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling, suggests a congenital condition.
The patient's asymmetric facial movement, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling, is consistent with unilateral facial paresis.
The patient's normal developmental milestones, uncomplicated pregnancy, and normal neurodevelopmental examination suggest a normal variant or benign condition.
The patient's facial asymmetry and abnormal lip movement could be consistent with Moebius syndrome, although the lack of other characteristic features makes this diagnosis less likely.

The inward deviation of the right lower lip when smiling or crying, despite normal facial movement at rest and normal neurodevelopmental examination, suggests a specific condition affecting the lower lip.

rationales.F02: The right lower lip deviates inward, suggesting unilateral facial weakness or paresis, which is more consistent with Congenital Facial Asymmetry or Unilateral Facial Paresis.
rationales.F06: The deviation of the right lower lip when smiling is consistent with Congenital Facial Asymmetry or Unilateral Facial Paresis, and less likely with Normal Variant or Moebius Syndrome.
rationales.F07: Symmetric frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth suggest that the facial weakness is limited to the lower lip, which is more consistent with Congenital Lower Lip Palsy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's facial asymmetry noted since birth, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling or crying, and symmetric facial movement at rest, supports Congenital Facial Asymmetry as the most fitting diagnosis.
